<!--
Purpose: show the diagnostics.py output for both processing vintages side by side,
  so the ocean-cell missing-value fix can be confirmed from the numbers.

Inputs:  ../output/missing_weather/missing_weather_summary.csv
         ../output/negative_rainfall/negative_rainfall_summary.csv
         ../output/missing_flow/missing_flow_summary.csv
         ../output/{missing_weather,negative_rainfall,missing_flow}/*.png
         ../output/taudem_flow/*.png
         Each summary CSV covers both vintages in one file, tagged by a `vintage`
         column. Each figure is a single file with one panel per vintage it covers,
         so this report includes it whole rather than pairing two files. The
         negative-rainfall suite is original-only and so has one panel.

Output:  ../output/report/report.html

Dependencies: rmarkdown, knitr, dplyr, readr (and pandoc)

Run from the repo root:
  Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("hydro/diagnostics/scripts/report.Rmd", output_dir = "hydro/diagnostics/output/report")'

Every number below is read from the CSVs written by diagnostics.py at render time.
Nothing is hardcoded, so a stale figure cannot survive a re-run.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(knitr)
```

```{r paths}
# The Rmd sits in scripts/; diagnostics.py writes to ../output/
OUT_ROOT <- normalizePath(file.path("..", "output"), mustWork = FALSE)
VINTAGES <- c("original", "test")

# One CSV per suite, both vintages inside it. A missing file means the suite has
# not been run yet.
read_suite <- function(suite, filename) {
  p <- file.path(OUT_ROOT, suite, filename)
  if (!file.exists(p)) return(NULL)
  read_csv(p, show_col_types = FALSE)
}

missing_weather <- read_suite("missing_weather", "missing_weather_summary.csv")
negative_rain   <- read_suite("negative_rainfall", "negative_rainfall_summary.csv")
missing_flow    <- read_suite("missing_flow", "missing_flow_summary.csv")

vintages_run <- if (is.null(missing_weather)) character(0) else sort(unique(missing_weather$vintage))
```

```{r helpers}
fmt_num <- function(x, digits = 1) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), "", format(round(x, digits), nsmall = digits, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))
}

fmt_int <- function(x) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), "", format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))
}

# Plain knitr::kable, deliberately. kableExtra does not install in the cluster's
# conda R -- its svglite dependency fails to compile -- and nothing here needs more
# than a table.
show_table <- function(data) {
  kable(data, format = "html", escape = FALSE)
}

# A chunk must not mix cat() with include_graphics(), so anything absent is
# collected here and listed once at the end rather than annotated inline.
MISSING_FIGS <- character(0)

fig <- function(relpath) {
  p <- file.path(OUT_ROOT, relpath)
  if (!file.exists(p)) {
    MISSING_FIGS <<- c(MISSING_FIGS, sprintf("`%s`", relpath))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  knitr::include_graphics(p)
}
```

The processed ERA5-Land monthly files exist in two vintages:

* **original** — `/project/cil/gcp/climate/ERA5-LAND/processed/monthly/`
* **test** — `.../monthly/test/`, rewritten so cells with no ERA5-Land value stay
  `NaN` instead of being converted to `0`

`diagnostics.py` runs the identical code over both, so every difference below is a
difference in the data rather than in the diagnostic. Each section reports how often
something occurs and where; none of them tries to explain why.

The rewrite also lengthened the record: every region covers more months in the test
vintage than in the original, and the start years are harmonized rather than varying
by region (see the Months / From / To columns below). Raw counts are therefore not
comparable across vintages — only the percentage columns are.

```{r vintage-status, results="asis"}
if (length(vintages_run) == 0) {
  cat("**No diagnostics output found.** Run `sbatch hydro/diagnostics/scripts/diagnostics.sh`",
      "before rendering this report.\n")
} else {
  cat(sprintf("Vintages in this render: **%s**.\n", paste(vintages_run, collapse = ", ")))
  if (length(vintages_run) < 2) {
    cat(sprintf("\nThe comparison is incomplete — `%s` has not been run.\n",
                paste(setdiff(VINTAGES, vintages_run), collapse = ", ")))
  }
}
```

# What the diagnostics show {.unnumbered}

* **The ocean fix works and is exact.** Every cell that was 0-filled in the original
  is NaN-masked in the test vintage, the land footprint is unchanged, and no cell
  ends up in a third state.
* **It propagates correctly into `rainfall_flow`.** In the original, 0-filled ocean
  routed exact zeros downstream, so the flow field appeared to cover open water; in
  the test vintage that ocean drops off the network. The coverage that disappears is
  the fix working.
* **No episodic missingness anywhere.** Neither vintage has a single cell that is
  missing in some months and present in others, so `rainfall_flow` missingness is
  entirely structural.
* **Negative rainfall looks like snowmelt, except in the tail.** Its geography and
  seasonality match the snowpack-residual explanation, but the most extreme negative
  values are far too large for that and need separate follow-up.

# Ocean masking

Region files are rectangular bounding boxes, so most cells in them are ocean. The
question is how those cells are marked. Three statuses are mutually exclusive:

* **all NaN** — no valid value in any month. This is the intended marking for ocean.
* **always zero** — has valid values, every one of them exactly `0`. This is the
  behaviour being fixed: a 0-filled ocean cell is indistinguishable from a genuinely
  dry land cell, and it drags means and flow accumulations toward zero.
* **has data** — at least one non-zero valid value.

```{r verdict, results="asis"}
if (is.null(missing_weather) || length(vintages_run) < 2) {
  cat("Both vintages are needed for a verdict; see the status note above.\n")
} else {
  v <- missing_weather %>%
    group_by(vintage) %>%
    summarise(regions = n(), always_zero = sum(n_always_zero),
              all_nan = sum(n_all_nan), has_data = sum(n_has_data), .groups = "drop")
  orig <- v %>% filter(vintage == "original")
  test <- v %>% filter(vintage == "test")

  cat(sprintf(
    paste0("Summed over the %s regional files, the original vintage marks **%s** ",
           "cells always-zero and **%s** all-NaN. The test vintage marks **%s** ",
           "always-zero and **%s** all-NaN.\n\n"),
    fmt_int(orig$regions), fmt_int(orig$always_zero), fmt_int(orig$all_nan),
    fmt_int(test$always_zero), fmt_int(test$all_nan)))

  if (test$always_zero == 0 && test$all_nan > orig$all_nan) {
    cat(sprintf(paste0("**Resolved.** No always-zero cells remain in the test ",
                       "vintage, and the cells that were 0-filled are now carried ",
                       "as missing. Cells with data: %s original, %s test.\n"),
                fmt_int(orig$has_data), fmt_int(test$has_data)))
  } else if (test$always_zero == 0) {
    cat("**Always-zero cells are gone from the test vintage**, but the all-NaN count",
        "did not rise above the original. Worth checking where those cells went",
        "before calling this resolved.\n")
  } else {
    cat(sprintf(paste0("**Not resolved.** The test vintage still has %s always-zero ",
                       "cells. See the per-region table for which regions.\n"),
                fmt_int(test$always_zero)))
  }
}
```

```{r coverage-note, results="asis"}
# The two vintages need not cover the same months. Where they do not, raw counts
# are not comparable between them and only the percentage columns are.
if (!is.null(missing_weather) && length(vintages_run) == 2) {
  n_diff <- missing_weather %>%
    group_by(region) %>%
    summarise(differs = n_distinct(n_time_steps) > 1, .groups = "drop") %>%
    pull(differs) %>% sum()
  if (n_diff > 0) {
    cat(sprintf(paste0("\nNote: **%d regions cover a different number of months ",
                       "in the two vintages** (see the Months column below). For ",
                       "those, compare percentages rather than counts.\n"), n_diff))
  } else {
    cat("\nBoth vintages cover the same months in every region, so counts are",
        "directly comparable.\n")
  }
}
```

## Per-region summary

```{r missing-weather-table}
if (!is.null(missing_weather)) {
  missing_weather %>%
    arrange(region, vintage) %>%
    transmute(
      Region = region,
      Vintage = vintage,
      Cells = fmt_int(n_cells),
      Months = fmt_int(n_time_steps),
      From = date_min,
      To = date_max,
      `All NaN` = fmt_int(n_all_nan),
      `% all NaN` = fmt_num(pct_all_nan),
      `Always zero` = fmt_int(n_always_zero),
      `% always zero` = fmt_num(pct_always_zero),
      `Has data` = fmt_int(n_has_data),
      `% has data` = fmt_num(pct_has_data)
    ) %>%
    show_table()
}
```

## Cell status

Original on the left, test on the right. The blue 0-filled ocean in the original
should become grey NaN-masked ocean in the test vintage, with the green land area
unchanged. Green territory changing between panels would mean the fix altered land
cells, which it should not.

```{r fig-cell-status, out.width="100%"}
fig("missing_weather/cell_status.png")
```

The map shows exactly the intended swap. Every blue cell in the original panel is
grey in the test panel and the green land footprint is identical between them, so
the fix relabelled ocean without touching a land cell. The status counts confirm
this is a clean one-for-one flip rather than an approximate one: the always-zero
total in the original and the all-NaN total in the test are the same number, the
original has no all-NaN cells at all, the test has no always-zero cells, and the
has-data count is unchanged.

Two things are worth noting about the original panel. The 0-filled area follows the
rectangular region boundaries, not the coastline, so the zeros were an artifact of
the bounding boxes rather than of anything physical. And because those cells carried
a valid `0` rather than a `NaN`, nothing downstream could have distinguished them
from genuinely rainless land — which is what the next two sections pick up.

# Negative rainfall

**Original vintage only.** The test vintage changed how ocean cells are marked, not
how rainfall is computed, so this check is unaffected by the fix and is not run as a
comparison.

Rainfall is a residual, `tp_total - snowchange`, so it goes negative when the monthly
increase in snow water equivalent exceeds total precipitation — for instance rain
that immediately freezes. Negatives are therefore expected in snow-affected cells.

`% cell-months negative` uses valid (non-`NaN`) cell-months as its denominator.

```{r negative-table}
if (!is.null(negative_rain)) {
  negative_rain %>%
    arrange(region) %>%
    transmute(
      Region = region,
      `Cells w/ negative` = fmt_int(n_cells_w_negative),
      `% cells w/ negative` = fmt_num(pct_cells_w_negative),
      `Min (mm/mo)` = fmt_num(min_neg_value_mm_mo, 2),
      `Median (mm/mo)` = fmt_num(median_neg_value_mm_mo, 2),
      `Mean (mm/mo)` = fmt_num(mean_neg_value_mm_mo, 2),
      `% cell-months negative` = fmt_num(pct_cell_months_neg, 3)
    ) %>%
    show_table()
}
```

Negatives are common as a share of cells but rare as a share of cell-months: the
`% cells w/ negative` column runs far higher than `% cell-months negative` in every
region, so this is a small number of months in a moderate number of cells rather
than a pervasive problem. The split across regions is what the snowmelt explanation
predicts — the snow-affected regions carry essentially all of it, and the two
tropical regions (`australia`, `mexico_south`) have no negative cells at all.

The `Median (mm/mo)` column is small, around a millimetre or two, which is the size
a snowpack-residual artifact should be. The `Min (mm/mo)` column is not: several
regions reach minima in the thousands of mm/month, which no monthly snowpack change
can produce. Those extremes are a separate issue from the ordinary negatives and are
worth tracing to individual cells before the series is used.

## Frequency

Color is the share of months with negative rainfall on a log scale, not the raw
count, so a cell negative in 10% of its months looks the same whether the record is
20 or 40 years.

```{r fig-neg-freq, out.width="60%"}
fig("negative_rainfall/negative_frequency.png")
```

The pattern is cryospheric, not random. Negatives concentrate in Alaska, northern
and western Canada, the Rockies and Cascades, the southern Andes, Scandinavia, the
Alps, the Caucasus, the Himalaya and Tibetan Plateau, and eastern Siberia — cold,
high, or both. The darkest cells, negative in something like a tenth of their
months, sit in the highest and coldest parts of that footprint, and the lowlands
around them fade to near-zero. Nothing appears in the warm tropics or the
subtropical deserts.

## Seasonality

Share of cells with data that are negative in each calendar month, averaged across
all years and regions.

```{r fig-neg-seasonal, out.width="60%"}
fig("negative_rainfall/negative_seasonal.png")
```

The seasonal cycle closes the argument. Negatives peak in December through February,
fall away sharply through March and April, sit at effectively zero from May through
September, and return in October and November — the Northern Hemisphere snow
accumulation season, which is where the regions above are. A defect in the
processing would not know what month it was, so the shape here is evidence that
these negatives are the expected `tp_total - snowchange` residual rather than a bug.
That does not extend to the extreme minima noted above.

# Missing rainfall_flow

`rainfall_flow` is monthly rainfall accumulated downstream through the TauDEM D8
network. A `NaN` means no routed value reached that cell that month. Cells `NaN` in
**every** month are off the network (ocean, or outside the DEM) and are expected;
they are excluded from the on-network denominators. The defect this check looks for
is the episodic case — a cell with a routed value in some months and not others.

Regional tiles overlap and are not deduplicated in this suite, so the unit
throughout is region × cell: a cell covered by two tiles is counted twice.

```{r flow-verdict, results="asis"}
if (is.null(missing_flow)) {
  cat("No flow output found; run the diagnostics before rendering.\n")
} else {
  f <- missing_flow %>%
    group_by(vintage) %>%
    summarise(episodic = sum(n_cells_episodic_missing),
              on_network = sum(n_cells_on_network), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(pct = episodic / on_network * 100)
  cat(paste0(sprintf("* **%s** — %s episodically-missing cells of %s on-network (%s%%)",
                     f$vintage, fmt_int(f$episodic), fmt_int(f$on_network),
                     fmt_num(f$pct, 4)),
             collapse = "\n"), "\n")

  # A cell should be off the network precisely when it has no rainfall to route, so
  # the on-network count should equal the rainfall check's has-data count. In the
  # original it does not, and that gap is the finding. Computed rather than asserted.
  if (!is.null(missing_weather)) {
    chk <- f %>%
      inner_join(missing_weather %>% group_by(vintage) %>%
                   summarise(has_data = sum(n_has_data), .groups = "drop"),
                 by = "vintage")
    cat("\nCells counted as on-network, against the cells the rainfall check found",
        "to have data:\n\n")
    cat(paste0(sprintf("* **%s** — %s on-network vs %s with data%s",
                       chk$vintage, fmt_int(chk$on_network), fmt_int(chk$has_data),
                       ifelse(chk$on_network == chk$has_data, ", identical",
                              " — the surplus is ocean the network still carries")),
               collapse = "\n"), "\n")
  }
}
```

## Per-region summary

```{r flow-table}
if (!is.null(missing_flow)) {
  missing_flow %>%
    arrange(region, vintage) %>%
    transmute(
      Region = region,
      Vintage = vintage,
      Months = fmt_int(n_time_steps),
      `Cells on network` = fmt_int(n_cells_on_network),
      `Cell-months` = fmt_int(n_cell_months),
      `Missing cell-months` = fmt_int(n_missing_cell_months),
      `% missing cell-months` = fmt_num(pct_missing_cell_months, 4),
      `Never missing` = fmt_int(n_cells_never_missing),
      `Always missing` = fmt_int(n_cells_always_missing),
      `Episodic` = fmt_int(n_cells_episodic_missing),
      `% on-net episodic` = fmt_num(pct_cells_on_net_episodic, 4)
    ) %>%
    show_table()
}
```

## Where the missing values are

Purple is missing in every month (off network), orange in some months only (the
defect).

```{r fig-flow-status, out.width="100%"}
fig("missing_flow/missing_flow_status_map.png")
```

There is no orange in either panel, and the episodic counts above are the reason:
not one cell in either vintage is missing in some months and present in others.
Whatever missingness `rainfall_flow`
has is a fixed property of a cell's position, not something that comes and goes, so
the episodic defect this check was built to find does not occur.

The two panels differ completely on everything else, and that difference is the
ocean fix showing up downstream. The original panel is uniformly grey — every cell
in every bounding box, ocean included, has a routed value in every month. That is
not a network that reaches the ocean; it is the 0-filled ocean cells routing exact
zeros through the accumulation, so the flow field looks complete while carrying
meaningless zeros over water. In the test panel the ocean is purple and drops off
the network, leaving grey only on land, and the on-network count collapses to the
land cells (see the counts above). Confirming the fix therefore means reading the
*loss* of coverage here as the desired outcome.

The `% missing cell-months` column in the table above should be read the same way:
its jump between vintages is ocean being correctly excluded, not data going missing.

Restricted to episodic cells, since always-missing ocean would otherwise saturate
the map and hide the cells that matter. When no vintage has any episodic cells — as
in the counts above — `diagnostics.py` skips this figure and it appears under
"Outputs not found" below. That is an empty result, not a broken one.

```{r fig-flow-freq, out.width="100%"}
fig("missing_flow/missing_flow_frequency_map.png")
```

# Accumulated flow network

From `vis_taudem.py`, on the test vintage `usa_monthly_flow.nc4`. A sanity check on
the routing rather than the rainfall: accumulation should grow downstream and trace
recognizable river channels.

```{r fig-usa-flow, out.width="100%"}
fig("taudem_flow/usa_rainfall_flow_map.png")
```

## Basin windows

Each panel shows mean `rainfall_flow`, peak `rainfall_flow`, and TauDEM's own
upstream cell count (`aread8`) over the same window, with gauge cities marked. The
three share a cell mask, so they cover identical cells. Since `rainfall_flow` is
`aread8` times mean upstream rainfall, the flow panels and the `aread8` panel should
pick out the same channels; they differ in shading because the first two are in mm
and the third is a cell count.

```{r fig-basin-panels, out.width="100%"}
panels <- sort(Sys.glob(file.path(OUT_ROOT, "taudem_flow", "flow_panel_*.png")))
if (length(panels) > 0) knitr::include_graphics(panels)
```

```{r basin-panels-note, results="asis"}
if (length(sort(Sys.glob(file.path(OUT_ROOT, "taudem_flow", "flow_panel_*.png")))) == 0) {
  cat("\n*No basin panels found. Run `sbatch hydro/diagnostics/scripts/vis_taudem.sh`.*\n")
}
```
